transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Dana. Could I get your account number and PIN to pull up your account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Dana, sure, account is 552-903-417, PIN 8810. This is Marcus Feldman.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks Marcus, that matches, you're verified. What can I help with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My mesh WiFi system, I've got three nodes set up, keeps dropping devices randomly. It's been a real problem this week specifically because I'm on video calls for work most of the day and it keeps cutting out mid-meeting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got it, so the three-node mesh system is dropping devices at random, and it's been especially disruptive this week because of back-to-back work video calls. Let's dig into this properly. When exactly did this start?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: About five days ago, so basically all week.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, five days. Does it happen on all devices, or mainly the one you're using for calls?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Mainly my work laptop honestly, my phone and the TV seem mostly fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a useful distinction, narrows things down.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, my phone and the TV have been totally fine through all of this, it's really isolated to the laptop.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good, that focuses things nicely. Is your laptop usually connected to the same mesh node, or does it roam between nodes depending on where you are in the house?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I mostly work from my home office, so it should be sticking to the node in that room.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah so what happens is I'll be mid-call and then out of nowhere the whole connection just—

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, it drops entirely for a few seconds and then comes back, yeah, that's a pretty classic sign of the mesh handing your laptop off between nodes even when it doesn't need to.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's actually exactly it, that's really frustrating because it happens at the worst possible moments, like right when I'm presenting something.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, let's check the node placement then. How far apart are your three nodes roughly?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: One's in the living room, one's in my office, and one's upstairs in the bedroom.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Honestly this has been such an issue this week because I've had to apologize to coworkers mid-meeting more than once, it's embarrassing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's check the signal overlap between the office node and the living room node then, since those are probably the two closest to where you actually work.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, how do I check that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open the mesh app, tap on your laptop under connected devices, and it should show a signal strength bar along with which node it's currently attached to.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me look... it says attached to the living room node right now, even though I'm sitting in my office.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That actually explains a lot, if it's latched onto the living room node instead of the much closer office node, you're going to get weaker signal and more frequent handoff attempts as it tries to decide whether to switch.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, that makes sense I guess, why would it pick the farther one though?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Mesh systems sometimes get sticky, once a device connects to a node it can be slow to hand off even when a closer node would be better, especially if the signal from the current node is still technically usable.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Got it. Is there a way to force it onto the closer node?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, we can do that. First, can you check if your mesh system has a setting called 'Client Steering' or 'Band Steering' enabled? It's usually under advanced network settings.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Checking... I see a toggle called 'Smart Connect', is that the same thing?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's likely it, most mesh brands bundle client steering and band steering under one umbrella setting like that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Actually wait, before we go further, I want to mention this whole week has just been a real problem for my work, I've had three calls drop completely, not just glitch, fully drop, and I had to call back in each time which looked pretty unprofessional on my end.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, let's check that Smart Connect setting, can you tell me if it's currently on or off?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alright, let's try turning that off temporarily, sometimes Smart Connect is actually the thing causing the stickiness rather than preventing it, since it's trying to manage the handoff logic itself and can get it wrong.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, turning it off now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Done.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let's manually disconnect and reconnect your laptop to WiFi so it re-evaluates which node to join fresh.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, disconnecting and reconnecting now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, reconnected, and now it shows attached to the office node.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, that's exactly what we wanted to see. Let's test it, can you do a quick video call test, even just to yourself or a test meeting link, and see how it holds for a few minutes?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, let me start one.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, that ran for a couple minutes with no drops, seems stable so far.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How did the audio and video quality look throughout, any stutter or freezing even without a full drop?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, actually really smooth the whole time, noticeably better than earlier this week.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a great sign, that means it's not just staying connected but staying connected with good quality too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a great sign. So to summarize, your laptop was stuck connected to the living room node instead of the much closer office node, and Smart Connect's own handoff logic was likely making that stickiness worse instead of better. Turning it off and forcing a fresh reconnect got it onto the right node.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That actually makes a lot of sense when you explain it that way.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I do want to say this has been a genuinely frustrating week, I nearly considered switching providers over this before calling in today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's check your plan speed real quick too, just to rule out bandwidth as a contributing factor alongside the node issue.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your plan supports plenty of speed for video calls even with several devices active, so that's not a factor here, this really was the node placement and Smart Connect combination.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to rule that out completely.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My partner also works from home some days, should I check which node their laptop is on too, just in case?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That would be a good idea, especially if they're ever in the office with you or nearby.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: They're usually in the bedroom upstairs actually, different room from me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, then it's worth a quick check on their end too, but since they're near the upstairs node directly, they're less likely to have the same stickiness problem you had.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes sense, I'll ask them to check anyway just to be safe.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good call, better to confirm than assume.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should I be worried about how old the mesh hardware itself is? We've had it a couple years now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A couple years is still well within normal lifespan for mesh hardware, and since firmware's current and the issue traced back to a software setting rather than the hardware itself, I wouldn't worry about age here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, wasn't looking forward to replacing the whole system if that was the case.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Understandable, and thankfully that's not where this landed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's also check if this same stickiness could affect your phone or the TV down the line, even though they seem fine right now, just so we're thorough.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you check what node your phone is currently attached to?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It shows the office node too, so that one's fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good, and the TV?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Living room node, but that makes sense since the TV's actually in the living room.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, that one's correctly placed then, no issue there.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should I turn Smart Connect back on now, or leave it off?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'd leave it off for now, at least for a few days, just to confirm the improvement holds without it. If everything's stable, you can decide later whether you want to try re-enabling it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'll leave it off then. How will I know if it's actually fixed versus just lucky today?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good question, I'd say if you get through a full work day of calls tomorrow with no drops, that's a strong signal. If it happens again, calling back in and mentioning we already ruled out Smart Connect and node placement will save a lot of time.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's a fair way to think about it, I'll keep track tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah so like I mentioned, the worst part was during a call with my director on Tuesday where the whole thing just cut out completely and I had to—

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Scramble to call back in and explain what happened, yeah, that's a rough spot to be in mid-meeting, especially with someone senior on the call.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly, it's just been a stressful week because of this honestly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's make sure we've covered everything on the technical side then. Are there any other devices in the house that seem to have connectivity issues, or is it really just been the laptop this week?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Really just been the laptop, everything else has been fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good, that's consistent with the node-stickiness theory then, since your laptop was the one on the wrong node the whole time.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Makes sense. Is there anything I should watch for with the other devices going forward?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not particularly, but if you ever add a new device or move furniture around, it's worth spot-checking which node things land on, just so nothing else gets stuck on a suboptimal one.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good tip, I'll keep that in mind.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should I check the other devices' node assignments periodically going forward, or is that overkill?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I wouldn't say it's necessary regularly, maybe just a quick glance every few months or whenever you notice something acting up, similar to what happened with your laptop.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That seems reasonable, I can build that into a habit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That should be plenty to catch anything early if it ever happens again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Out of curiosity, is there a way to just manually assign a device to a specific node instead of relying on it figuring it out automatically?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Some mesh systems support that, let me check your specific model.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yours doesn't support manual node pinning unfortunately, it's fully automatic, but the fix we just did, disabling Smart Connect and forcing a reconnect, should be enough to keep it on the right node without that feature.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, good to know either way.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there a firmware update I should check for on the mesh system, just to rule that out too?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good thought, let's check.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: All three nodes are showing current firmware, so that's not a factor here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, one less thing to worry about.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This has genuinely been one of the more frustrating tech issues I've dealt with, just because of the timing with work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's also set a reminder on the account to check back on this in a week, just so it's tracked properly on our side.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, that works.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Done, I've noted the node-stickiness fix and the plan to leave Smart Connect off for now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Appreciate that. Should I be concerned this could happen with a different node next time?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's possible in theory if a device roams and gets sticky again, but now you know exactly what to check, which node a device is on and whether Smart Connect is contributing, so it'll be a much faster fix if it ever recurs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's reassuring, thank you for walking through all of that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: One more thing, does a full mesh reboot ever help versus just the single device reconnect we did?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It can, especially if multiple devices are affected, but since this was isolated to just your laptop, the targeted reconnect was the more precise fix, no need for a full system reboot this time.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know the difference for next time.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there a limit to how many devices can be on the mesh at once? I've been adding a lot of smart home stuff lately.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your model supports up to fifty connected devices across all three nodes, so you've got plenty of headroom for more smart home additions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, I've been adding one every few months it feels like.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's pretty normal these days, the system should handle it fine as long as node placement stays reasonable.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Speaking of smart home stuff, could any of those devices have contributed to the stickiness issue in the first place?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's possible in general, more devices can add some background chatter, but in your case the timing and pattern really pointed specifically to the node handoff and Smart Connect setting rather than device count.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, good to have that confirmed rather than just guessing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Do you recommend spacing out where I add new smart devices, or does it not really matter which node they connect to?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Generally it's fine, most smart home devices are low-bandwidth, it's really primarily video-heavy devices like laptops and streaming boxes where node placement matters most.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's helpful context, I was overthinking that a bit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Totally understandable given the week you've had with this.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Since we're on the topic, would it be worth adding a fourth node for better coverage, given how spread out the house is?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It could help with overall coverage, but I wouldn't say it's necessary just for this specific issue, since the real problem was the stickiness and Smart Connect setting, not a coverage gap.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fair enough, I don't want to spend money on something that wouldn't actually fix anything.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly, I'd hold off on that unless you start noticing actual dead zones somewhere in the house.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good advice, I'll keep an eye out for that separately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there any kind of priority setting I could put on my laptop specifically, since it's the one used for work calls?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes actually, most mesh systems have a Quality of Service or device priority setting, let's check if yours has that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, checking... yeah, there's a 'Device Priority' section.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, go ahead and add your laptop there and set it to high priority, that'll help make sure it gets bandwidth preference over other devices during video calls.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, added it and set to high.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great, that's a nice extra layer of protection on top of the node fix we already made.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes me feel a lot better about tomorrow's calls honestly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that priority setting affect other people in the house if they're streaming or gaming while I'm on a call?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It can give your laptop preference during contention, but it's not an aggressive cap on others, they'd just yield a bit of bandwidth during your call windows if things get busy.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, that seems like a reasonable trade-off.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly, it's meant to be a light touch, not a hard restriction on everyone else.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know. Is this priority setting something I could have found myself, or was that pretty buried too?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's a little buried, most people don't dig into that menu unless they're specifically troubleshooting something like this.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Makes sense, wouldn't have thought to look there on my own.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the mesh system log which devices used the most bandwidth, in case I want to see what else might be competing with my calls?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, there's a usage breakdown under the main dashboard, it'll show relative bandwidth by device over the last 24 hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh that's actually useful, I'll check that out later.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's a good way to spot anything unexpectedly hogging bandwidth if this ever comes up again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good tip, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: While I've got you, does the mesh system support a separate guest network? I've been meaning to set one up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, under network settings there should be a 'Guest Network' toggle, it creates an isolated network so guests can't see your other devices.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh nice, let me check... found it, turning it on now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Done, it's on with a separate password.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, that's a nice added layer of security for anyone visiting who needs WiFi.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, I've been meaning to do that for a while.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the guest network share the same bandwidth pool, or is it separate?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Same pool, but it's isolated at the device level, so it won't interfere with the priority setting we just put on your laptop.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, that's exactly what I was hoping to hear.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: One more, is there a way to get notified if the mesh system itself goes down, not just individual devices?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, under notifications there's a 'System Health Alerts' toggle, want me to walk you through turning that on?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, please.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go to app settings, then Notifications, then System Health Alerts near the top.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Found it, turning it on.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Done.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great, now if any node goes fully offline you'll get a push notification instead of just noticing devices dropping.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's really helpful, wish I'd had that on this week honestly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good thing we're getting it set up now then.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that notification also cover WiFi password changes or anything security related?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's specifically for node connectivity and system health, password changes would show as a separate confirmation when you make them yourself, not really something that needs a push alert.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fair enough, that makes sense.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there a way to see historical uptime for the whole mesh system, like a percentage over the month?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, under the dashboard there's an uptime stat, let's check what it's showing for this month.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looks like 97 percent this month, which reflects the drops from this week, should trend back up now that the fix is in place.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good, that's a nice concrete way to track whether this actually holds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly, feel free to check back on that number in a few weeks to confirm the improvement.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will do, thank you for all of this, genuinely.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Makes sense. I think that covers the technical side.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we wrap up, is there anything else going on with the network, or was this really just the laptop this week?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Just the laptop, everything else has been solid.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Anything else I can help you with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I think that's everything, thank you Dana.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you so much, Marcus. We do value your feedback, so please stay on the line after this call for a short survey. Thank you for choosing S-Net, have a great rest of your day.
